title: Some Interesting Things You Didn't Know About Stephen Hawking
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant, with guest producer Matt, profile physicist Stephen Hawking. They open with a shout-out to the Cooperative for Education (CoEd) scholarship sponsors, then cover Hawking's Nobel Prize omission, his birth date and Galileo coincidence, his ALS diagnosis at age 21 and Lou Gehrig's disease, his rowing as Oxford coxswain, his school years and Oxford studies, his cosmology work and the "boundless universe" idea with Jim Hartle, his marriage to Jane and later to nurse Elaine Mason with allegations of abuse, a tabloid claim about a California sex club that Oxford denied, black holes and his bet with John Preskill, the Georgie children's book trilogy with daughter Lucy, his views on alien life and time travel, and honors such as the Lucasian chair. The episode closes with listener mail from Dan about using peak oil talk to clear a bar at last call.

entities.name: Georgie's Secret Key to the Universe

segments.title: Opening banter and CoEd scholarship shout-outs
segments.summary: Brief sponsor read for the Toyota Corolla, then the hosts thank new CoEd scholarship sponsors for supporting education for Guatemalan schoolchildren and introduce the Hawking topic.

segments.title: Hawking's early life, Nobel omission and ALS diagnosis
segments.summary: The hosts note Hawking has never won a Nobel Prize, mention his birth date and the Galileo death anniversary coincidence, and describe his ALS diagnosis at age 21 while at Oxford, the disease's course, and how he has lived with it.

segments.title: Oxford rowing, school years and choosing cosmology
segments.summary: Hawking was Oxford's rowing coxswain, a role that also steers the boat, and was an average student in grade school, where classmates nicknamed him Einstein. His father wanted him to be a doctor, but he chose physics and cosmology over biology.

segments.title: Boundless universe theory and the Big Bang
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Hawking's work with Jim Hartle on a finite but boundless universe, combining Feynman's quantum approach with Einstein's relativity, and a proposed collapse of spacetime in about twenty billion years. The hosts say the article's explanation was a rough interpretation.

segments.title: Marriages to Jane and Elaine Mason, and abuse allegations
segments.summary: The hosts describe Hawking's first wife Jane, whom he married after his diagnosis, their divorce in the mid-1990s, and his marriage to nurse Elaine Mason. They relay reported allegations of abuse and control, which the hosts attribute to a Vanity Fair article.

segments.title: Sex club rumor and Hawking's wit
segments.summary: A report said Hawking was a frequent visitor to a California sex club. Oxford denied it, saying he went once as a friend's guest. The hosts note his charm and his quip that women are a total mystery to him.

segments.title: Black holes and the Hawking-Preskill bet
segments.summary: The hosts explain how black holes form when stars collapse, and describe the bet between Hawking and John Preskill over whether information escapes black holes. Hawking conceded that Preskill was right, and the stake was an encyclopedia.

segments.title: Georgie children's book trilogy with Lucy Hawking
segments.summary: Hawking co-wrote a children's book trilogy with his daughter Lucy, beginning with Georgie's Secret Key to the Universe in 2007, followed by George's Cosmic Treasure Hunt and George and the Big Bang in 2011, which introduce physics to children.
topics: Georgie's Secret Key to the Universe

segments.title: Alien life, time travel and honors
segments.summary: Hawking has said publicly that alien life may exist, possibly intelligent and not DNA-based, and supports panspermia. He believes in time travel forward in time. He held the Lucasian Professorship at Cambridge, once held by Isaac Newton, and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom and CBE.

segments.title: Listener mail: peak oil at last call
segments.summary: Listener Dan from New York describes using a peak oil discussion to clear customers out of his East Harlem bar at last call. The hosts thank him and ask for new uses of the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts invite listeners to share new uses for the show on social media and email, point to the website, and close with a sponsor read.
